A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same target-feasibility evaluator study. The complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison; relocated material can be matched.

before.justification: v7 reports original experiments with Skipper, LEAP, and Dyna on SSM and RDS, non-singleton target evaluations, and preliminary Atari results.

after.justification: v9 retains these original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendices A–J, including the ablations and preliminary Atari findings.

M1.justification: The update rule in Equation 2, C51-style distributional evaluator, generate and pertask relabeling, and DreamerV2 adaptation remain unchanged. The replacement citation for C51 does not indicate an architecture change.

E1.justification: Both versions retain SSM and RDS, their OOD scenarios, singleton and non-singleton targets, and the preliminary Atari100k evaluation. No training or evaluation coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same Skipper, LEAP, Dyna, and relabeling comparisons, including the episode comparator for non-singleton targets. The newly cited C-learning work is not added as an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Training budgets, task sizes, task sampling, OOD difficulties, and testing procedures are unchanged. Section 5.1.2 clarifies that expected-distance estimation errors serve as a feasibility-convergence proxy; the previously evaluated quantity and plotted metrics remain the same.

E4.justification: The generator-hallucination analyses, relabeling ablations, distance-dependent errors, and OOD performance breakdowns in Appendices A–G are retained. Figure 2 illustrates the same cases despite its revised presentation.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 20 independent seed runs and 95% confidence intervals for the presented mean curves. No repeated-run or uncertainty-reporting procedure changes.

E6.justification: The experimental plots in Figures 4–7 and 9–19 retain the same results and trends, with no result entries added or removed. Appendix J still reports negligible Atari100k performance gains and approximate convergence of the distance estimates.

T1.justification: Result 4.1 is renamed Theorem 4.1 without changing its statement or adding a proof. Equation 1 moves the horizon parameter between superscripts and arguments equivalently; the feasibility definitions, update rule, and mathematical reasoning remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The four central contributions remain target categorization, evaluator desiderata, the combined learning architecture and relabeling solution, and empirical reductions in delusional planning. The broader introductory wording and rewritten conclusion retain the substance of these claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 now conditions fast evaluation on using lightweight evaluators instead of broadly asserting that the evaluator is lightweight. Section 5.1.2 explicitly interprets distance errors as a proxy, and Section 7 clarifies the existing applicability boundary by describing excluded targets as action-like.

D1.justification: The implementation details in Appendices H–J, evaluator configuration, relabeling proportions, rejection threshold, and code-access disclosures are retained. No new implementation settings or resource-availability changes are documented.

R1.justification: The C51 citation changes from Dabney et al. (2018) to Bellemare et al. (2017), and Eysenbach et al. (2021) is added to the relabeling discussion. Nair et al. (2018) and Sutton and Barto (2018) are removed. The main related-work positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The abstract and much of the introduction are rewritten, alongside substantial editing of the preliminaries and conclusion. Terminology, explanatory wording, and several headings change, and the Impact Statement is removed. This is extensive editorial revision despite the stable scientific content and section sequence.

P2.justification: Figure 2's legend and labels are redesigned, Figure 1's caption and Table 1's headings are revised, and Appendix Part I is rearranged: Figure 8 precedes Table 2, while Table 3 receives a separate page. The experimental displays themselves are retained.

improvement.justification: v9 makes the distinction between formal feasibility and its distance-error proxy more explicit and qualifies the runtime discussion, providing limited gains in precision and exposition. The scientific evidence and substantive limitations remain unchanged. Appendix displays are less compactly arranged, but this does not outweigh those modest clarity improvements.
